carlos (customer): Hi team — after yesterday's model pin my embeddings suddenly increased from 1024 -> 1536 dimensions. Existing index is now misaligned and a bunch of requests are failing with a schema error. Any idea what changed?

maya (support): sorry about that — can you paste the raw response you get from /v1/embeddings (obscure any keys)? also which model id are you calling and did you pin a version?

carlos (customer): here's the curl and response:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings \\\\  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-xxx" \\\\  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\\\  -d '{"model":"embed-l2","input":"hello world"}'
```
response (trimmed):
```json
{"object":"embedding","model":"embed-l2","usage":{"tokens":3},"data":[{"embedding":[0.001,0.002,...(total 1536 floats)..., -0.003]}]}
```
Errors in our app: "vector length mismatch: expected 1024, got 1536". We pinned via console yesterday to "embed-l2:stable" because of latency regression.

maya (support): thanks — tagging @olivia and @dmitri. Can you also share the request_id from the response headers? (x-request-id or x-rw-id)

carlos (customer): header x-rw-id: rw_20250304_7f2b9a

olivia (ml): looking. Quick hypothesis: the pinned alias may have been remapped to a newer variant of the embed family that changed hidden-dim. We rolled a canary of embed-l2 variants last week that switched from base-1024 -> wider-1536 for better semantic coverage. Pinning "embed-l2:stable" might point to a floating alias rather than an immutable model digest.

dmitri (eng): confirmed in routing logs for rw_20250304_7f2b9a — model binding used model_id "embed-l2@v20250303" which is the new wider variant. The pin in console saved the alias but the alias target was updated by the canary rollout.

maya (support): OK — options: 1) we can revert alias to the previous digest (temporary) so your traffic sees 1024 again, 2) we can create a compatibility shim on your side (truncate/pad to 1024), or 3) migrate index to 1536. Which do you prefer?

carlos (customer): we have a large index, can't reindex quickly. Option 1 preferred, but need it ASAP and we need to be sure it won't flip again.

olivia (ml): we can pin to an immutable model digest id instead of the floating alias. Example API to pin to a digest:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/models/pin \\\\  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-ops" \\\\  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\\\  -d '{"alias":"customer/carlos-prod","model_digest":"embed-l2@sha256:abc123def456"}'
```
That will bind the alias to the old digest and stop future canary remaps. We'll perform the revert for you if you confirm timeframe.

dmitri (eng): I've queued a rollback of the alias mapping to the previous digest. ETA ~10 minutes. We'll also add a guard so alias updates require an explicit immutable-digest promotion for org-level pins. :eyes:

maya (support): doing the revert now, carlos — I'll update when complete. Also setting an ops ticket to make pinning behavior clearer in console docs.

deploy-bot: alias-update rw-deploy:embed-l2 -> embed-l2@sha256:abc123def456 by dmitri (eng) at 2025-03-04T17:22:11Z :rocket:

maya (support): done — can you retry the same curl and confirm you now get 1024-length embedding?

carlos (customer): retried: confirmed vector length 1024, errors cleared. Huge thanks. Please add a note in our account that we need immutable pins for production.

olivia (ml): noted. We'll follow up with a postmortem on the canary mapping logic and update the console UI to label pins as "floating alias" vs "immutable digest".

maya (support): assigning follow-up ticket SUP-5482 to implement console and docs changes and to notify affected customers about the canary semantics.

carlos (customer): appreciated. one last question — is there a quick client-side check we should add to detect dimension drift?

dmitri (eng): yes — validate embedding.length against your stored index vector_size on every ingest call and fail fast with a clear message. As a temporary measure you can detect >1024 and reject until we confirm. We'll also add a response header `x-model-vector-dim` in the next patch so it's explicit.

carlos (customer): perfect, thanks everyone :pray:

maya (support): glad it's resolved. Leaving this thread open for any follow-ups.
note: thread about unexpected embedding vector size change after alias pinning/canary remap
